Quick read + recommended mapping below (notes from product and listings):

Proposal (tl;dr): create a two-tier offering surfaced as a single public SKU with optional cloud-variant entitlements. This keeps marketing/partner-friendly metadata while allowing technical gating where needed.

Mapping suggestion:
- Redwood Standard (public SKU) — available on AWS/Azure/GCP in US + EU immediately. Includes standard throughput profile (shared pooling, quantized medium).
- Redwood Local (variant entitlement) — for APAC markets; initially available on GCP and Azure for countries where we can guarantee KMS/local keys + audit logging.
- AWS APAC gating — AWS asks we either show AWS listing as "Available in selected APAC regions" or delay APAC until we confirm co-sell commit (recommended: require 6-month dedicated commit to unlock full APAC).

Product constraints to call out:
- Quantization/latency parity: APAC on small-instance types will increase tail latency; must document in listing.
- KV cache persistence: Dedicated pools needed for high-throughput customers (affects co-sell scoring).
- Packaging metadata: marketplace descriptions must include minimum throughput and supported sequence lengths — I've drafted copy in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2BskusMatrix

Attachments: updated sheet (skus_v2.xlsx) with proposed region-by-cloud columns and a simple cost-model (cost-models.csv).

Recommendation: adopt hybrid. Move quickly on GCP/Azure APAC exposure; gate AWS APAC until commit is secured.

Owner: Marissa — product copy + region matrix
Action: Marissa to update the Drive doc and share final copy by Fri 14 Aug EOD.

-Marissa
Director, Product GTM | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AWS/Co-sell: SKU + region gating for ACME opportunity

Couple of practical points from listings/ops side:
- Marketplace metadata differences: Azure wants per-SKU entitlement tags (metering plan) at submission time; GCP is more flexible but requires service account details for APAC regions.
- Co-sell scoring: AWS gives higher uplift when SKU maps to a specific pricing tier with commit-backed discounts — that aligns with Marissa's "require 6-month commit" recommendation.
- Billing & trials: If we surface one public SKU, we need clear metering toggles (trial vs paid) per cloud. That will add ~5 biz days per cloud for listing QA.
- Regional pricing: Azure mandates local-currency display in some APAC markets (India, Japan). We'll need legal sign-off on price parity and tax implications.

Operational ask: if we gate AWS APAC on a reserved commit, we should add a flag in the listing metadata and a fallback description so customers in non-enabled regions see a clear call-to-action (contact sales). I can implement the flag once Marissa provides final matrix.

Owner: Karthik — listing metadata implementation and QA (ETA 6 business days after final copy)

-Karthik
Listings & Marketplace Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SKU routing & APAC gating decision for multi-cloud listings — decision and next steps

Thanks for the quick turn — good alignment. Decision and next steps below.

Decision (final):
- Public listing model: single public SKU "Redwood Standard" with two published variants/entitlements. This keeps the marketing path simple and preserves co-sell eligibility.
- Variant mapping:
  * Redwood Standard (default): available US + EU on AWS/Azure/GCP at launch.
  * Redwood Local (APAC variant): enabled initially on GCP + Azure for a tight APAC country list (Japan, Singapore, Australia, South Korea).
- AWS APAC gating: AWS listing will show APAC as "coming soon" until we secure a 6-month reserved commit / dedicated pool for APAC. This is required to meet AWS co-sell pricing band.

Rationale: the hybrid approach minimizes operational friction for marketing and partner routing while addressing data locality and performance constraints in APAC. It preserves the fastest path to listing on GCP/Azure and keeps AWS co-sell upside but protected behind a clear commercial gate.

Action items & owners:
- Marissa: finalize listing copy + region matrix and publish final Drive doc (ETA: today EOD). Also prepare short customer-facing FAQ for APAC gating.
- Karthik: implement listing metadata flags and QA plan (ETA: 6 biz days after Marissa publish).
- Kimberly: prepare sales play (talk track for ACME + co-sell ask) and draft the dedicated-commit short-form agreement we will present to AWS (ETA: Tue 18 Aug).
- Vivek: coordinate with Lina/Rajesh to confirm the co-sell uplift mechanics once we have commit language (I'll own that outreach).

Attachments: skus_v2.xlsx, cost-models.csv (see Drive for final).

Let's keep the HubSpot deal HS-8891 updated with the gating decision and the required next steps. Marissa/Karthik — please add your deliverables as tasks in the deal record.

Cheers,
Vivek
Head of GTM Strategy | Redwood Inference
